def: The process by which green plants use sunlight to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose (sugar) and oxygen.
1. (formal) to breathe. 2. (biology) for a plant or animal to take in oxygen from air or water and release carbon dioxide.
The scientific study of plants.
1. the scientific study of the relationship between living things and their environment. 2. the pattern of relations between a particular group of organisms and their environment.
All the living things in an area and the way they affect each other and the environment.
Not harmful to the environment; designed to cause as little harm as possible to the environment.
Plants in general, or the plants that are found in a particular place.
1. a plant whose leaves, flowers or seeds are used to give flavour to food, or as medicine. 2. (also herb /hɜːb/) a soft, leafy plant without woody stems.
1. (noun) a plant that lives for several years (compare annual, biennial). 2. (adjective) lasting for a long time; happening again and again.
The study and practice of growing plants, flowers and fruit.
1. a living thing, especially one that is very small. 2. a system consisting of parts that depend on each other.
1. the scientific study of the way in which genes control the development of living things. 2. the genes of a particular living thing.
1. a process in which the genetic material of a person, animal or plant changes in structure, especially when it is passed on to the next generation. 2. a change in the form or nature of something.
a change, especially in amount, level or form; a different form of something.
the quality or fact of including many different types of people or things; the range of different types.
The process of producing a hybrid, especially by combining the genetic material of two different plants or animals.
To put something or somebody into a particular class or category according to its type.
1. (of people, animals, plants) to produce young. 2. to make a copy of something; to be copied.
1. to develop gradually, especially from a simple to a more complex form. 2. to develop a plan, idea, etc. in this way.
To change frequently; to rise and fall irregularly.
1. to prepare and use land for growing plants. 2. to develop a skill, an ability, a feeling, etc. 3. to try to develop a friendship or a relationship with somebody.
1. to plant or scatter seeds in or on the ground. 2. (figurative) to introduce or spread feelings or ideas.
1. the time of year when crops are cut and gathered from the fields. 2. the crops cut and gathered. 3. (verb) to cut and gather a crop. 4. (figurative) the result of an action.
1. to pull or pick something, especially with the fingers. 2. to remove the feathers from a chicken or other bird. 3. (figurative) to pull somebody out of a dangerous or unpleasant situation.
1. to choose somebody or something from a group. 2. to take flowers, fruit, etc. from the plant or tree by hand. 3. to remove small pieces of something from a surface.

1. (noun) the total amount of crops, profits, etc. produced. 2. (noun, finance) the income from an investment. 3. (verb) to produce a result, profit, etc. 4. (verb) to give way to pressure or persuasion.
1. (verb) to care for young children or animals until they are fully grown. 2. (verb) to breed or grow animals or plants. 3. (adjective, only before noun) at the back of something.
(of land) suitable or used for growing crops.
1. (noun) a large farming implement with blades, used to turn the soil and make it ready for planting. 2. (verb) to turn over the surface of soil using a plough.
A tool with a sharp metal blade and a long handle, used for digging.
1. a garden tool with a long handle and a row of metal prongs at the end. 2. (verb) to gather leaves or smooth soil with a rake.
1. (noun) a pile of things, one on top of another. 2. (verb) to put things into a pile. 3. (informal) a large amount of something.
1. a large untidy pile of things. 2. (informal) a large amount of something. 3. (informal, especially NAmE) an old, broken car.
1. a number of things tied or wrapped together. 2. a collection of things. 3. (informal) a large amount of money.
1. a number of things of the same type, fastened or growing together. 2. a small group of people. 3. (informal) thanks a bunch (= thank you, often sarcastic).
A container, usually tall and made of glass or pottery, used for displaying cut flowers.
The light from the sun.
Any plant without leaves, flowers or green colouring, often growing on other plants or on decaying matter, e.g. mushrooms, mould, yeast.

1. a soft green or grey fungus that grows on old food or damp objects. 2. a hollow container used to give shape to a liquid or soft substance. 3. (verb) to shape a soft substance into a particular form.
Fine powder produced by the male part of a flower, used in fertilising other flowers.
1. (of a seed) to start growing, producing roots and shoots. 2. (of a plant) to produce roots and shoots.
1. (noun) the small, hard part of a plant, from which a new plant grows. 2. (verb) to plant seeds. 3. (idiom) go to seed — to become weaker or untidy.
To begin to grow or develop rapidly; to flourish.
1. (noun) a small, tight part that grows on a plant and from which a flower or leaf develops. 2. (verb) to produce buds.
1. (noun) the coloured part of a plant, often with a smell, from which seeds or fruit develop. 2. (verb) to produce flowers.
1. (noun) a flower, or the mass of flowers on a tree. 2. (verb) to open into flowers. 3. (figurative) to develop and become successful.
1. (noun) a flower, especially one that is bright and beautiful. 2. (verb) to have flowers; to be in flower. 3. (figurative) a state of beauty, health or success.
1. (noun) a pleasant smell. 2. the smell left behind by an animal or person. 3. (verb) to give something a particular smell.
Having a strong, pleasant smell.
1. to become ripe. 2. to make something ripe.
1. (noun, countable / uncountable) the part of a plant that contains seeds, often eaten as food. 2. (noun) the result of an action. 3. (verb) to produce fruit.
1. (of a plant) to become dry and shrivelled. 2. to make a plant dry and shrivelled.
1. to be broken down into simpler substances by the action of bacteria, fungi, etc. 2. to make something do this. 3. to rot or decay.
1. (verb) to decay slowly because of the action of bacteria, fungi, etc. 2. (noun) the process of decaying. 3. (informal) nonsense.
1. (verb) to become gradually damaged, weaker, or worse. 2. (noun) the process of decaying.
1. (of food) no longer fresh. 2. no longer interesting because it has been repeated too often. 3. (of air) not fresh.
A chemical compound whose molecule contains two atoms of oxygen.
1. to take land back for use. 2. to recover a material so it can be used again.
(of a plant) flowering when the day is shorter than a critical length.
Able to grow in conditions with less than full sunlight.
A thick forest with tall trees, found in tropical areas with heavy rainfall.
1. a thick forest in a tropical area. 2. (informal) a place that is very confusing or out of control.
1. a large area of land where crops such as tea, coffee, sugar, or rubber are grown. 2. an area where trees are planted for wood.
1. an area of land used for growing crops or keeping animals. 2. a subject or area of study or work. Verb: (in cricket, baseball) to catch or stop the ball.
1. a flat area cut from a slope where crops can be grown. 2. a row of houses joined together. Verb: to build a flat area on a slope.
Wood that is used for building or making things.
1. a black substance made by burning wood slowly in an enclosed space, used for fuel or art. 2. a dark grey colour.
1. a long thick piece of wood from a tree. 2. a record of events. Verb: 1. to cut down trees. 2. to make a record.
A printed design or picture that is used by an organisation or company to identify its products.
The science or practice of planting and taking care of trees and forests.
1. a part of a tree that grows out from the trunk. 2. a local office of a company or bank. 3. a part of a subject. Verb: to divide into branches.
1. the main part of a tree. 2. the long nose of an elephant. 3. a large strong box for storing or transporting things. 4. (US) the boot of a car.
A large branch of a tree.
1. the part of a plant that grows under the ground. 2. the cause or origin of something. 3. (grammar) the basic form of a word. Verb: to make a plant grow roots.
Grass that has been cut and dried, used as food for animals.
1. the dry stems of plants such as wheat, used as bedding for animals. 2. a thin tube for drinking.
1. a tall plant that grows in or near water. 2. a small piece of cane or metal that vibrates in a musical instrument.
1. a small sharp pointed part on the stem of a plant such as a rose. 2. a tree with thorns.
1. a wild plant growing where it is not wanted, especially among crops or garden plants. 2. (informal) marijuana. Verb: to remove weeds.
1. a common wild plant with thin green leaves that covers the ground. 2. (slang) marijuana. 3. (informal) a person who informs on others.
A field of grass, used for making hay.
An area of ground covered with short grass, usually in a garden or park.
1. a small green or black fruit with a bitter taste, used for food and for oil. 2. (also olive tree) the tree on which this fruit grows. 3. (also olive green) a yellowish-green colour.
1. an evergreen tree with needles and cones. 2. (also pinewood) the wood of this tree. Verb: (literary) to feel a deep sadness.
1. a plant that climbs up a wall or along the ground. 2. (also grapevine) a plant that produces grapes.
1. a small plant with purple or white flowers that bloom in spring. 2. a bluish-purple colour. Adjective: bluish-purple.
A plant that grows from a bulb, with large brightly coloured flowers in spring.
1. a herb whose leaves are used for flavouring food. 2. a place where coins are made. Verb: to make a coin. 3. (informal) a large amount of money.
A long line of rocks or sand near the surface of the sea.
A very simple plant that lives in or near water and has no real leaves, stems or roots.
A substance produced by living cells that causes a chemical change without being changed itself.
1. (chemistry) a substance that makes a chemical reaction happen faster. 2. (figurative) a person or thing that causes change.
1. to let somebody/something come out of a place. 2. to make a film, song, etc. available. 3. to stop holding something. Noun: the act of releasing.
1. the act of sending out gas, heat, light, etc. 2. gas, heat, or light that is sent out.
1. to take in a liquid, gas, or other substance. 2. (figurative) to take in information. 3. to use up time, money, or effort.
1. the movement of blood around the body. 2. the movement of air, water, or goods. 3. the average number of copies of a newspaper or magazine sold.
To be greater than a number or amount.
1. the process of absorbing something. 2. the speed or rate at which something is accepted.
A substance that is needed for growth and health.
1. the ability to do work; the power that comes from food, electricity, etc. 2. the enthusiasm and determination to do things.
Everything that is around a place; the environment.
1. a system of parts in a machine that work together. 2. a method or process for achieving something.
To have an equal but opposite effect to something, so that a balance is kept.
To keep somebody/something safe from harm, injury, or damage.
1. to keep something in its original or existing state. 2. to treat food so that it can be kept for a long time.
1. the protection of plants, animals, natural areas, etc. 2. the careful use of something such as energy or water.
A fire in the bush or forest, especially in Australia.
1. (formal) to make a fire stop burning. 2. to end an idea, feeling, etc.
To destroy something (especially in a controlled way).
1. to damage or spoil something completely. 2. to cause somebody to lose money or social position. Noun: 1. (plural) the remains of a building that has been damaged. 2. the process of being ruined.
1. (formal) to die. 2. to be destroyed or lost.
1. to pull or knock down a building. 2. (informal) to eat something very quickly. 3. (figurative) to defeat somebody easily.
To break a law, rule, or agreement.
1. to make something weaker gradually. 2. to dig under something to make it fall.
1. the state or process of a species, family, or larger group becoming extinct. 2. the process of putting out a fire.
1. a regular way in which something happens or is done. 2. a design of lines, shapes, or colours. Verb: to form a pattern.
A thing that is a result or consequence of an action, situation, etc.
1. the effect that a person, event, or situation has on somebody/something. 2. the act of one object hitting another. Verb: /ɪmˈpækt/ to have a strong effect.
Connected with a particular season; happening or needed during a season.
1. based on new ideas or methods that are not yet proved. 2. connected with scientific experiments.
1. showing that you like or approve of something. 2. (formal) making people have a good opinion. 3. (formal) giving you an advantage.
1. producing or able to produce large amounts of goods or crops. 2. (of land) producing good crops.
1. producing the result that is wanted. 2. (of a law, system, etc.) having an effect.
1. doing something well without wasting time, money, or energy. 2. (of a machine or system) working well.
Great in amount, size, or importance.
1. extremely large, heavy, or solid. 2. (informal) very successful or popular.
Extremely large or great.
As great or as large as possible.
As small or as little as possible.
Best; most favourable.
